newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut t-bill issue raises 324.1 bln pounds.
newsitem.headline: Beirut t-bill issue raises 324.1 bln pounds.

text.p: Lebanon's weekly treasury bill issue of March 13 raised 324.1 billion Lebanese pounds after the Bank of Lebanon restricted sales of most bills.
The previous issue raised 272.9 billion pounds.
The issue posted a nominal surplus of subscription against maturity of 110.1 billion pounds. It raised the following amounts (in billion of pounds, previous week in brackets):

The central bank said only five percent of all competitive bids -- those made by Lebanese institutions -- were accepted up to the discount rate and yield for three-month bills and seven percent for six-month bills. It was five percent for 12-month and also six percent for two-year bills.

The Bank also restricted the acceptance of non-competitive bids -- those made by private individuals and foreign investors -- for three- and six-month bills. It approved only five percent up to the discount rate and yield for three-month bills and seven percent for six-month bills.
However, all non-competitive bids for 12-month and 24-month bills were accepted, the Bank said.
The Lebanese pound closed at 1,546.75 to the U.S. dollar on Monday from $1,547.25 a week earlier and 1,585.5 a year ago.
